lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
Date of birth: 21 Jul 1998 | Nationality: Indian
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Feb 2021 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator that tightens the previous bound by a log factor; it is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability and writes the problem sets, earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Pioneered a data-driven, research-first approach to volatility modeling that delivered robust, actionable insights.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch
Methods: time-series econometrics, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: Make sure the code link is live, clickable, and shows relevant work.
Consider adding a portfolio or LinkedIn link if you maintain one.
items.because: It could be useful.

items.says: Remove the date of birth and nationality.
items.because: They do not help establish qualifications and can introduce bias.

items.says: Make sure “Ph.D. candidate” accurately reflects your formal status.
items.because: The title is appropriate only if you have reached formal candidacy.

items.says: Consider adding a concise research focus.
items.because: It could strengthen your fit for the roles you’re targeting.

items.says: Add honors or distinctions if you have relevant ones to report.
Define “risk-adjusted returns” and what the 35% compares against.
items.because: The performance claim needs a clear metric and baseline.

items.says: Give the evaluation period and say whether the result was out of sample and after costs.
items.because: Those details make the performance claim interpretable.

items.says: Distinguish the 35% result from the later Sharpe increase.
items.because: The section presents a separate performance claim that may describe the same result.

items.says: Qualify the claim that every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
items.because: It is too absolute, especially given the 400-configuration selection.

items.says: Specify how tuning was separated from reported test results.
items.because: The evaluation design needs to be described accurately.

items.says: Add the feature store’s tools or stack if useful.
Clarify what reuse in two later signal projects means.
items.because: The claim should be substantiated.

items.says: Clarify whether the allocation went live or was only approved for a future period.
Quantify “small” if disclosure is allowed.
items.because: “Small” is vague.

items.says: Do not present the best of 400 backtested configurations as the expected live Sharpe.
items.because: Selecting the maximum creates multiple-testing bias, so it is not a sound estimate of live performance.

items.says: Clarify whether this is the same signal or result as the 35% claim and the Kaggle bullet.
items.because: The repeated order-book and Sharpe claims could look like double-counting.

items.says: Explain what the starting and ending Sharpe measure, whether they are annualized, the test period, and how costs were handled.
items.because: The performance claim needs to be interpretable.

items.says: Explain whether the Sharpe increase came from the signal alone or the broader book.
items.because: The result’s attribution is unclear.

items.says: Check and accurately describe the random-stream setup rather than simply claiming the same seed on every worker.
items.because: Workers generating the same stream may make runs non-independent and undermine the study.

items.says: Clarify the comparison behind “tightens the previous bound by a log factor.”
Ensure the paper’s “under review” status is current and does not imply acceptance.
Fix the tense mismatch between “Taught” and “writes.”
items.because: The teaching activity is described in the past tense but writing problem sets in the present.

items.says: Specify what the 4.8/5 teaching rating measures.
items.because: Its context may not be obvious.

items.says: Identify or link the R package.
Verify the 3,000-download figure and make its time period clear.
items.because: The figure should come from a reliable source.

items.says: Replace the promotional wording with a specific, verifiable contribution.
items.because: It does not tell the reader what you did or found.

items.says: Say which forecasts or benchmarks were compared and give the evaluation period.
Clarify whether the crisis periods were part of the same testing plan and what each reported result covers.
items.because: The phrase about 24 indices and both crisis periods is ambiguous.

items.says: Account for multiple comparisons across all reported tests.
De-emphasize the working paper’s page count.
items.because: It is less important than the paper and presentation.

items.says: Add a link if the working paper is shareable.
Make the work’s status clear.
Add a concrete contribution or result, such as placement or an evaluation outcome.
items.because: The bullet is too general to show what you contributed or how the competition went.

items.says: Define what the 0.02 gap represents and whether it narrowed or disappeared.
Describe precisely what changed in validation when leakage was corrected.
items.because: Correcting leakage can change validation scores rather than simply improve them.

items.says: Remove the order-book result if it is the Northpeak work, or clearly distinguish the project, signal, data, and evaluation period.
items.because: It appears to duplicate the Northpeak result and could look like double-counting.

items.says: Add relevant tools you can genuinely use.
items.because: The programming list is short for a quantitative research résumé.

items.says: Consider adding methods relevant to the target roles and demonstrated elsewhere in the résumé.
Keep date, location, separator, and punctuation formatting consistent throughout.
